privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how The Golden Circle Consulting LLC ("we," "us," or "Beauty Hub Pro") collects, uses, shares, and protects information when you visit our website, use our salon and spa management platform, or interact with the marketing and transactional communications we send on behalf of our customers.

s1.p1: Beauty Hub Pro is the software arm of The Golden Circle Consulting LLC, a Florida limited liability company. Throughout this policy, references to "the Platform" or "the Service" mean the Beauty Hub Pro web application, client portal, and related Cloud Functions, regardless of whether they are accessed at beautyhubpro.com or a white-label domain operated by one of our customers (for example, crm.your-salon.com).
s1.p2: When you are a customer's client (for example, a client of a salon that uses our Platform), our customer (not Beauty Hub Pro) is the controller of your personal data, and we act as a processor. This Privacy Policy describes the practices Beauty Hub Pro follows in either role.

items21: Account information: name, email address, phone number, organization name, role, and password (stored hashed).
Quote-request information: business size, current software, contact details, and free-text notes you submit through our public quote form.

Customer organization data: client records, appointments, treatments, packages, products, invoices, waivers, intake forms, agreements, photographs uploaded to forms, signatures captured in-app, and other operational data you enter into the Platform.
Communications: the content of messages you send us or that you send through the Platform to your clients.
items22: Device and usage data: IP address, browser type, operating system, device identifiers, language preference, referring URL, pages visited, and timestamps.
Cookies and similar technologies: see Section 9 for details.
Authentication signals: session tokens, sign-in timestamps, and idle activity events used to enforce the 60-minute session timeout.
items23: Identity providers: when you sign in with Google or via phone OTP, the identity provider shares the identifiers you authorize (typically email or phone number).
Scheduling integrations: when our customer connects Acuity Scheduling, we receive appointment and client records that Acuity sends over its webhook or that we fetch via Acuity's API.
Payment and messaging providers: we receive operational metadata from Twilio, Infobip, Resend, and similar providers (delivery status, error codes), but we do not handle credit-card data directly.

s3.p: We use the information described above to:
items: Operate, secure, and improve the Platform;
Provision accounts, authenticate users, and enforce role-based access;
Process bookings, package consumption, invoices, and the transactional messages tied to those actions;
Send marketing and operational communications you have requested or that our customer has configured (subject to opt-out; see Section 6);
Provide customer support, onboarding, data migration, and consulting services;
Detect, prevent, and respond to fraud, abuse, security incidents, and rule violations;
Comply with applicable law, court orders, and regulatory obligations.

s4.h: 4. Legal bases for processing (GDPR / UK GDPR)
s4.p: Where European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Swiss data protection law applies, we rely on the following legal bases:
items: Contract: to provide the Platform you or your organization signed up for.
Legitimate interests: to secure the Platform, prevent abuse, improve product quality, and conduct direct marketing to existing business customers, balanced against your rights.
Consent: for non-essential cookies, marketing emails to non-customers, and any processing requiring explicit opt-in.
Legal obligation: to retain records, respond to lawful requests, and meet tax and accounting requirements.

s5.p: We do not sell personal information. We share information in the following limited ways:
items: Sub-processors and infrastructure providers who help us operate the Platform; see Section 7 for a current list.
Our customers (the salons, spas, and studios on the Platform) where you are their client. They control your data within their organization's tenant.
Professional advisers (lawyers, accountants, auditors) under confidentiality.
Business transfers: in connection with a merger, acquisition, financing, or sale of assets, subject to the new entity continuing to honor this policy.
Legal compliance: when we believe in good faith that disclosure is necessary to comply with law, protect rights and safety, or respond to lawful requests.

s6.p1: We send marketing email to people who have asked to hear from us or whose organization is a current Beauty Hub Pro customer. You can opt out at any time by clicking "unsubscribe" in any marketing email or by emailing us. Transactional emails (account, security, billing) cannot be unsubscribed while you have an active account.
s6.p2: Marketing and transactional SMS sent through the Platform are governed by our <sms>SMS Terms</sms>, including the STOP / HELP keyword behavior required by US carriers. We do not buy or sell phone numbers for marketing, and we do not use phone numbers for advertising on third-party platforms.

s7.p1: We rely on the following sub-processors to provide the Platform:
items: Google Cloud / Firebase: hosting, authentication, Firestore database, Cloud Functions, Cloud Storage (United States).
Twilio, Inc.: SMS delivery in the United States and other supported countries.
Infobip Ltd.: SMS delivery as an alternative to Twilio.
Resend (Resend Inc.): transactional and marketing email delivery.
Acuity Scheduling (Squarespace, Inc.): calendar sync, optional per organization.
Google Drive (Google LLC): automatic backup of signed waivers and issued invoices when a customer enables Drive backup.
s7.p2: Each sub-processor processes personal data only on documented instructions, under written contracts that require appropriate technical and organizational measures. We review this list periodically; updates will be reflected in this Section with an updated "Last updated" date at the top of this policy.

s8.p: We are based in the United States, and our infrastructure providers process data primarily in the United States. If you access the Platform from outside the United States, your information will be transferred to and processed in the United States. Where required, we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses, supplementary measures, or the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (where applicable) to lawfully transfer personal data out of the EEA, UK, or Switzerland.

s9.p1: We use the following categories of cookies and local storage:
items: Strictly necessary: authentication, security, idle-timeout coordination across tabs, CSRF protection. Cannot be disabled.
Functional: user preferences such as language and theme.
Analytics: aggregated usage metrics so we can prioritize what to build. Set only with consent.
Marketing: we do not place advertising cookies on the public site at this time.
s9.p2: You can manage your choices through the cookie banner the first time you visit, or by clearing site data in your browser. Strictly necessary cookies cannot be refused without disabling parts of the Platform.

s10.p: We retain personal data for as long as needed to provide the Platform and comply with our legal obligations. Account data is retained for the life of the account and for up to twelve (12) months after termination so customers can reactivate without losing history. Auditable records (invoices, signed waivers, audit logs) are retained for a minimum of seven (7) years to meet tax and recordkeeping obligations, even after account termination, unless a shorter retention is required by law.

s11.p1: Depending on where you live, you may have the following rights with respect to your personal data:
items: Access a copy of the personal data we hold about you;
Correct inaccurate data;
Delete personal data (subject to retention obligations);
Restrict or object to certain processing;
Receive your data in a portable format;
Withdraw consent where processing relies on consent;
Not be discriminated against for exercising your rights (CCPA / CPRA);
Lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (GDPR / UK GDPR).
s11.p2: If you are a client of one of our customers, please direct rights requests to that customer first; they are the controller of your data inside their tenant. We will assist them in honoring your request. For requests about data we control directly (for example, account holders, quote requesters, marketing recipients), contact us using the details in Section 14.

s12.p: The Platform is intended for use by businesses and the adult clients of those businesses. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children under the age of thirteen (13), or under the age of sixteen (16) where applicable in the EEA, without parental consent. If you believe a child has provided personal data to us without appropriate consent, contact us and we will delete it.

s13.p: We implement industry-standard administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect personal data, including: per-tenant data isolation enforced at the database rule layer, encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest, role-based access control with audit logs, OTP-gated signing flows for sensitive documents, rate-limiting on outbound paid services, and routine security review. No system is perfectly secure; you use the Platform at your own risk and should keep your account credentials confidential.

s14.p: For privacy questions, requests, or complaints, contact us at:
items: Email: <email>thegoldencircle.skincare@gmail.com</email>
Phone: <phone>+1 754-232-6590</phone>
Postal: The Golden Circle Consulting LLC, State of Florida, United States

s15.p: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Material changes will be flagged on the Platform or by email to account holders. The "Last updated" date at the top of this page indicates when the latest version took effect. Your continued use of the Platform after changes take effect constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

dpa.title: Data Processing Addendum
dpa.intro: This Data Processing Addendum ("DPA") forms part of the <terms>Terms of Use</terms> between The Golden Circle Consulting LLC ("we," "us," or "Processor") and the organization that uses the Beauty Hub Pro platform ("you," "Customer," or "Controller"). It governs how we process personal data on your behalf when you use the Platform to manage your clients, appointments, forms, and communications.

s1.p: For personal data relating to your clients and contained in Customer Data, you are the controller and we are the processor (or, where applicable, the "service provider" under U.S. state privacy laws). For data we collect about your account and your authorized users, we act as a controller as described in our Privacy Policy. This DPA applies only to our processing as a processor on your behalf.

s2.p: We will process personal data only (a) to provide and support the Platform, (b) in accordance with your documented lawful instructions (including those given through the Platform's features and settings), and (c) as required by applicable law. The subject matter, duration, nature, and purpose of the processing, the types of personal data, and the categories of data subjects are described in Annex A.

s3.p: You are responsible for establishing a lawful basis for the personal data you upload, for providing any required notices to your clients, and for obtaining any required consents (including for marketing communications sent through the Platform). You must not provide us with special categories of data or regulated health data except as permitted by the <terms>Terms of Use</terms> (which prohibit using the Platform for HIPAA-regulated Protected Health Information absent a separate Business Associate Agreement).

s4.p: We ensure that personnel authorized to process personal data are bound by appropriate obligations of confidentiality and process personal data only on our instructions.

s5.p: We implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures designed to protect personal data, including: encryption in transit and at rest, per-tenant data isolation enforced at the database rule layer, role-based access controls, audit logging, rate-limiting on outbound services, and routine security review. These measures are described in more detail in our <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> and may be updated to maintain or improve the level of protection.

s6.p: You authorize us to engage the sub-processors listed in Annex B to process personal data on our behalf. We impose data-protection obligations on each sub-processor that are no less protective than those in this DPA, and we remain responsible for their performance. We will give you a reasonable means to learn of changes to our sub-processor list (for example, by updating Annex B and the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy>) so you may object on reasonable data-protection grounds.

s7.p: We process personal data primarily in the United States. Where we transfer personal data originating in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or Switzerland to a country without an adequacy decision, we rely on an appropriate transfer mechanism, such as the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses (and the UK Addendum, where applicable), which are incorporated into this DPA by reference where they apply.

s8.p: Taking into account the nature of the processing, we will provide reasonable assistance to help you (a) respond to requests from data subjects to exercise their rights, (b) meet your security, breach-notification, and data-protection-impact-assessment obligations, and (c) consult with supervisory authorities where required. The Platform's self-service features (export, edit, delete) are the primary means by which you can fulfill many data-subject requests directly.

s9.p: We will notify you without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting your Customer Data, and will provide information reasonably available to us to help you meet your own notification obligations. Our notification is not an acknowledgment of fault or liability.

s10.p: Upon termination of the Platform services, we will, at your choice, delete or return your Customer Data, and delete existing copies, except to the extent retention is required by law or by the retention schedule described in our <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> (for example, auditable invoice and signed-form records).

s11.p: We will make available information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with this DPA and will allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by you or an auditor you mandate, subject to reasonable confidentiality, scheduling, scope, and frequency limitations.

s12.p: Each party's liability under this DPA is subject to the limitations and exclusions of liability in the <terms>Terms of Use</terms>. This DPA takes effect when you begin using the Platform and continues for as long as we process personal data on your behalf.

aup.title: Acceptable Use Policy
aup.intro: This Acceptable Use Policy ("AUP") describes how you may and may not use the Beauty Hub Pro platform, websites, and related services. It is incorporated into and forms part of our <terms>Terms of Use</terms>. Capitalized terms not defined here have the meanings given in the Terms of Use.

s1.p: You are responsible for everything that happens through your account. This AUP applies to you, your employees, your contractors, any users you provision under your account, and any end clients you grant access through the Platform. If you become aware of any violation by anyone using your account, you must stop it immediately and tell us.

s2.p: You may not use the Platform to upload, transmit, store, share, or send messages that:
items: Are unlawful, fraudulent, defamatory, obscene, pornographic, hateful, or discriminatory;
Promote or facilitate violence, self-harm, terrorism, human trafficking, or child sexual abuse material;
Infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property, privacy, publicity, or other right of any person;
Contain malware, ransomware, spyware, or any other malicious code;
Disclose another person's confidential or personal information without their consent;
Are intended to deceive recipients about the identity of the sender or the nature of the message.

s3.p: You may not send SMS, email, or other messages through the Platform that:
items: Are unsolicited, unwanted, or sent without the recipient's prior express consent, in violation of the TCPA, CAN-SPAM Act, GDPR, or any other applicable law;
Are sent to numbers or addresses obtained from a purchased, scraped, or rented list;
Disregard a STOP, UNSUBSCRIBE, opt-out request, or any equivalent;
Misrepresent the sender, the content, or the purpose of the message;
Promote prohibited content categories under carrier rules (such as cannabis, gambling, payday loans, or "get rich quick" schemes) without proper carrier registration and pre-approval;
Are sent at a frequency or in a manner that violates carrier policies or our <sms>SMS Terms</sms>.
Access the Platform other than through the interfaces we provide (including scraping, crawling, or reverse engineering);
Probe, scan, or test the vulnerability of the Platform or attempt to bypass authentication, authorization, or rate limits, except under a coordinated, written security testing agreement with us;
Interfere with the proper functioning of the Platform, including by denial-of-service, traffic floods, or excessive automated calls;
Use the Platform to host or distribute content unrelated to your salon, spa, or wellness business;
Resell, sublicense, or expose the Platform to third parties outside your organization, except for your normal end clients;
Use the Platform to build, train, or benchmark a competing product or service;
Remove or alter any copyright, trademark, or other proprietary notice in the Platform.

Have all rights and consents necessary to upload, store, and process the Customer Data you put into the Platform, including the rights to send marketing communications to the contacts in your audience;
Keep your records of consent and provide them to us within fifteen (15) days of a written request;
Delete records that are no longer needed and respond promptly to data subject access, deletion, and correction requests from your end clients;

Not use the Platform to store Protected Health Information (PHI) as a HIPAA covered entity or business associate unless you have a signed Business Associate Agreement with us. The Platform is not HIPAA-compliant by default (see Section 5 of the <terms>Terms of Use</terms>);
Not share login credentials between users. Every staff member must have their own account so role and audit trails are accurate.

s6.p: You must protect the security of your account and the Customer Data inside it. This includes using strong, unique passwords, enabling and protecting multi-factor or OTP flows where offered, promptly removing access for departing staff, and reporting suspected unauthorized access to us within forty-eight (48) hours.

s7.p: If you become aware of a violation of this AUP, whether by you, your team, your end clients, or any third party, report it to <email>thegoldencircle.skincare@gmail.com</email>. We will investigate reports in good faith and may take action consistent with this AUP and the <terms>Terms of Use</terms>.

s8.p1: We may investigate any suspected violation of this AUP, and we may, in our sole discretion, take any of the following actions without prior notice:
items: Require corrective action;
Temporarily or permanently suspend access to all or part of the Platform;
Remove or restrict access to specific content;
Terminate the account;
Cooperate with law enforcement.
s8.p2: Where practical and where it does not increase risk to other customers or end clients, we will first contact the account admin and provide an opportunity to cure. We are not required to give notice in cases of serious violation, abuse, illegal activity, or risk to the Platform.

s9.p: We may update this AUP from time to time. The "Last updated" date at the top of this page indicates when the latest version took effect.

sms.title: SMS / Mobile Messaging Terms
sms.intro: These SMS Terms describe how Beauty Hub Pro and the businesses that use our Platform send text messages. They apply to both transactional messages (such as appointment confirmations and waiver links) and marketing messages. By providing a phone number to a Beauty Hub Pro customer or by texting a covered short code or long code, you agree to these SMS Terms.

s1.p: Beauty Hub Pro is a software platform. Messages sent through the Platform are sent on behalf of our customers (salons, spas, and similar businesses). The business that collects your phone number is the sender from your perspective; Beauty Hub Pro provides the technology that delivers the message through carrier partners such as Twilio, Inc. and Infobip Ltd.

s2.p1: Before you receive marketing SMS through the Platform, the sending business must obtain your prior express written consent. By providing your mobile number to a business and opting in (whether on a paper form, online form, or by texting a designated keyword), you consent to receive SMS messages from that business at the number you provided. Consent is not a condition of purchase.
s2.p2: For transactional messages (appointment confirmations, reminders, waiver links, OTP codes, package expiry notices), the business may text you because you have an active relationship with them, even if you have not opted into marketing. You may opt out of marketing while continuing to receive transactional messages.

s3.p: Message frequency varies by business and message type. Typical volumes include:
items: Transactional: one message per booking, plus occasional reminders or follow-ups.
Marketing: the sending business sets the cadence, typically no more than four (4) messages per month per customer, but you should refer to the business's own messaging policy for specifics.

s4.p: Message and data rates may apply. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.

s5.p1: You can interact with messages sent through the Platform using standard keywords:
